tasks.title: Total one order
tasks.description:
Implement `orderTotal(order)` under `// Task 1` in `src/reports.js`.

Return the order's total in cents:

- add up `qty * priceCents` for every entry in `order.items`
- subtract `order.discountCents` when the order has one
- the total never goes below `0`

An order with no items totals `0`.
nextSteps: Read the example order at the top of `src/reports.js`.
Add up the items with `reduce`, starting from 0.
Take the discount off and make sure the result cannot go negative.
Run `node src/demo.js` and check the first two lines.
hints: This is one value made from a whole array. Which array method is built for that?
Not every order has `discountCents`. Reading a missing field gives `undefined`, and `undefined` in arithmetic gives `NaN`.
Compute the subtotal with reduce, subtract the discount (or 0 when there is none), then keep the larger of that and 0.

tasks.title: Find the best sellers
tasks.description:
Implement `topCandles(orders, n)` under `// Task 2` in `src/reports.js`.

Count the units sold per sku, skipping orders whose `status` is `'cancelled'`. Return an array of `{ sku, units }` for the `n` skus with the most units:

- most units first
- on a tie, the sku that comes first alphabetically goes first
- if fewer than `n` skus were sold, return all of them
nextSteps: Count units per sku in an object or a `Map`.
Turn the counts into `{ sku, units }` objects and sort them.
Keep the first `n` with `slice` and run the demo.
hints: There are three steps here: filter, count, rank. Write them one after another instead of all at once.
A `Map` from sku to units makes counting easy: read the old count (or 0), add qty, write it back.
Your sort compare function needs two rules. When `b.units - a.units` is 0, fall back to comparing the two skus as strings.

tasks.title: Revenue per day
tasks.description:
Implement `revenueByDay(orders)` under `// Task 3` in `src/reports.js`.

Return an object that maps each day to that day's revenue in cents, for example `{ '2026-11-02': 3200 }`.

- only orders with `status` `'paid'` count
- the day is the date part of `placedAt` (its first 10 characters)
- an order's revenue is its total with the discount taken off, so `orderTotal` from Task 1 helps
- days without paid orders do not appear
nextSteps: Loop over the orders and skip the ones that are not paid.
Cut the day out of `placedAt` and add the order's total to that key.
Run the demo and compare with the orders in `src/orders.js`.
hints: This is grouping: many orders go into one bucket per day. An object whose keys are dates is the bucket.
The first time you see a day its key is missing, so add to `days[day] ?? 0` instead of `days[day]`.
